newsitem.title: USA: Aronex says inhibitor shows good results.
newsitem.headline: Aronex says inhibitor shows good results.

text.p: Aronex Pharmaceuticals Inc said on Tuesday that its inhibitor compound, known as Zintevir, had shown excellent safety results in both animal studies and in Phase I clinical trials at dose levels that show anti-HIV activity in vitro.

Two papers published in the September issue of the Journal of Pharmacology and Experimental Therapeutics offer data from single- and multi-dose intravenous studies in monkeys, showing Zintevir was extremely well tolerated at a range of doses from 2.5 to 50 mg/kg.

A Phase I clinical trial involving single, rising doses from 0.75 mg/kg to 3 mg/kg in HIV-positive patients supported preclinical results, showing no clinically significant adverse effects, the company said.
Pharmacokinetic data from the Phase I trial indicate that plasma concentrations exceeding in vitro inhibitory concentrations are achieved for periods exceeding six hours.
Zintevir is currently undergoing a dose-escalation study in HIV-positive patients in which safety, pharmacokinetics and viral load are being evaluated.
